datasets.name: An open fMRI resource for studying human brain function and covert consciousness under anesthesia
datasets.context: graded propofol sedation with responsive and loss-of-responsiveness periods

published_isd_method.roi_description: 400 Schaefer cortical parcels plus 56 Tian subcortical parcels
published_isd_method.segregation_adjustment: subtract first mode after matrix eigendecomposition

datasets.best_use: first reproducibility target for the published propofol fMRI ISD analysis, followed by exploratory subject-grouped predictions of behavioural responsiveness
limitations: 26 participants is a small cohort for flexible machine learning
behavioural unresponsiveness is not equivalent to absence of phenomenal experience
task-related neural processing is not a direct subjective report
the dataset and published ISD analyses have already been described publicly; evaluation is reproduction/secondary analysis, not a blind replication
The 2026 WJ repeatability analysis uses this same ds006623 cohort; it is a same-dataset methodological comparator, not independent replication
The reported WJ within-condition floor is protocol- and segment-length-specific and must not be treated as a universal threshold

secondary_reanalysis.paper_title: Architectural reorganization of functional connectivity after propofol anesthesia exceeds within-state measurement variability and is only marginally reversed during early recovery

datasets.name: A repeated awakening study exploring the capacity of complexity measures to capture dreaming during propofol sedation
datasets.channels: 65-channel 10-10 layout as listed by the NEMAR catalogue
datasets.best_use: secondary repeated-awakening study with report-aligned EEG complexity and perturbation analyses
datasets.acquisition_strategy: prefer NEMAR Zarr remote slice access or the smallest subject/session/task subset; do not fetch the 77.3 GB archive by default
preconditions: inspect the v1.0.0 Zarr root attributes for licence, citation and source commit
preserve attribution conservatively while licence statements disagree
verify event/report timing and which recordings include TMS
limitations: 21 participants; recordings and windows are not independent participants
dream report, recall and absence of recall are distinct outcomes
TMS-present and TMS-absent recordings must not be pooled without an explicit design
do not redistribute raw data or derived participant-level data until terms are reconciled

datasets.name: Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness
datasets.version: published_release; exact portal snapshot to be frozen at intake
datasets.best_use: exact reproduction of the published COGITATE Experiment 1 fMRI cross-task stimulus-category decoding on the N=73 replication phase, followed by separate participant-held-out/site-transfer and RCAF measurement-quality extensions
datasets.holdout_status: published_results_are_public; not a new blind holdout
limitations: acquisition/cohort counts, quality-controlled paper analysis counts and current public release counts are distinct denominators
paper quality-controlled fMRI and MEG cohorts are 108 and 97; optimization/replication subsets are 35/73 and 32/65 respectively
paper iEEG cohort is endpoint-dependent: 34 recruited, two excluded for incomplete data, and a specific identity-RDM analysis reports 29 after further completion filtering
public release documentation reports 118 fMRI, 100 MEG/EEG and 38 iEEG records; release presence does not imply inclusion in the primary published analysis
optimization and replication phase membership must be frozen from participant-level metadata or the exact supplementary mapping, never inferred by random repartition
published outcomes have been inspected; subsequent analysis is reproduction or secondary analysis, not a blind holdout
The 2026 Bryant-Whyte 246-statistic analysis uses the same COGITATE MEG source cohort; it is a same-dataset method comparator, not independent replication
Its 35,280 candidate-model fits create a model-selection problem; winning measures must be re-evaluated inside nested participant-grouped validation and untouched confirmation
BIDS M-EEG release availability is distinct from raw/unprocessed M-EEG availability; V1.3 lists the latter as a future release
The article's supplementary PDF was corrected on 2026-10-15; use the corrected supplement and paper version

Final article cites Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.18294156 (empirical.zip/model.zip), while the author README still points to older preprint support data at 10.5281/zenodo.15315238 (data.zip); treat archives as distinct until file manifests are reconciled
The article states pyspi 1.1.0 but the author requirements file pins 1.1.1; 1.1.1 changes TLMI directionality, so run both and compare against archived CSVs

Author code imputes missing values from the selected participant table before grouped CV when missingness is below 10%; quantify this separately with fold-local imputation without rewriting the historical reproduction

paper_phase_counts.ieeg: no optimization-versus-replication split; analyse endpoint-specific participant flow

access.license: CC BY 4.0 as stated by COGITATE data release
access.access_note: Data are openly licensed but download portal access requires a user account; verify exact bundle DOI/version and terms at intake

fmri_experiment_1.note: Official introduction states raw/unprocessed and BIDS fMRI Experiment 1 are released.

meeg_experiment_1.bids: prior versioned M-EEG releases V1.0 (batch 1) and V1.2 (batch 2); 2026 Bryant-Whyte analysis confirms use of BIDS MEG data for 100 participants
meeg_experiment_1.raw_unprocessed: V1.3 introduction lists raw/unprocessed batch 1 and batch 2 as future releases
meeg_experiment_1.note: Do not conflate BIDS availability with raw/unprocessed availability. For a new intake, verify exact BIDS bundle, participant manifest, source commit, terms and checksums.

ieeg.note: The cohort is 38 in the current catalogue; inspect exact release bundle and terms before intake.

experiment_2.note: Raw/BIDS fMRI and M-EEG formats are listed as future releases.

primary_reproduction_phase.endpoint: cross-task stimulus-category decoding across task-relevant and task-irrelevant conditions

datasets.construct_warning: task-irrelevant is not an unconscious label; stimulus decoding is not a universal consciousness detector

secondary_meg_reanalysis.title: A data-driven approach to identifying and evaluating connectivity-based neural correlates of conscious visual perception

correction.note: Corrected supplement replaces earlier PDF; corrected equation and tables must be used.

findings_summary.task_relevance_accuracy_upper_bound: no candidate measure exceeded 0.56 in reported analysis
findings_summary.fold_variability: marked variability; authors emphasize relative trends over absolute accuracy
findings_summary.theory_interpretation: tentative; not strong evidence of necessity or sufficiency of either theory

validation_design.cross_task: train one relevance context, test the other, same participants N=94; context transfer, not unseen-participant validation

preprocessing_audit.finding: author classifier imputes <10% missing values with feature mean on selected full participant table before grouped CV
preprocessing_audit.interpretation: reproducing historical code and testing a corrected sensitivity are separate lanes

datasets.name: Sleep-EDF used by Project Hypnos
datasets.best_use: sleep-stage classification and reproducibility of the two-subject pilot
limitations: sleep-stage labels are not ground truth for phenomenal consciousness
the historical pilot reports two subjects only and must not be described as clinical validation
dataset release, EDF files, annotation version and file checksums must be pinned before a new analysis

datasets.name: Modeling an auditory stimulated brain under altered states of consciousness using the generalized Ising model
datasets.population: healthy adult volunteers; published cohort summary reports mean age approximately 24 years
datasets.context: propofol sedation with awake, light sedation, deep sedation and recovery acquisitions
datasets.best_use: locked independent-cohort/site transportability test after the ds006623 reproduction pipeline, using resting-state awake-versus-deep-sedation as the primary comparable contrast and auditory listening as a separate task-specific analysis
limitations: 17 participants is a small external cohort; participant-level uncertainty must be emphasized and flexible machine-learning models are not justified by this sample size
published analyses have excluded participants for motion in some condition-specific comparisons; actual retained denominators must be recomputed from the frozen QC protocol before inference
rest and auditory-listening acquisitions must be analysed separately and must not be pooled as if they were exchangeable
task content differs from ds006623 mental-imagery and hand-squeeze tasks, so task-specific results are not direct replications of those paradigms
sedation state, behavioural responsiveness, task processing and subjective experience are separate variables; this dataset does not provide a universal consciousness label
external confirmation must be performed with a frozen pipeline and no tuning on ds003171 outcomes

external_validation_plan.analysis_rule: Keep rest and auditory-listening analyses separate; lock ROI/edge mapping, preprocessing, estimator, comparator, exclusions and thresholds on ds006623 before opening ds003171 outcomes. Do not apply PFM-NSI to the released NIfTI inputs as if they directly satisfy its CIFTI/fsLR input contract; record NSI as not assessed unless a separately validated compatible input is obtained.

available_data_formats: diffusion NIfTI files (.nii.gz) with bval/bvec sidecars
task events TSV and JSON sidecars

pfm_nsi_compatibility.inspected_release_tree: OpenNeuro ds003171 v2.0.1 GitHub release tree (534 files; complete tree response)
pfm_nsi_compatibility.observed_input: BOLD NIfTI (.nii.gz); no CIFTI .dtseries.nii files in the inspected release tree
pfm_nsi_compatibility.pfm_nsi_default_contract: CIFTI dtseries.nii on fsLR-32k; optional fsaverage6 input is resampled to packaged fsLR-32k resources and requires Connectome Workbench
pfm_nsi_compatibility.disposition: Do not claim NSI has been applied. A NIfTI-to-CIFTI/surface mapping would need its own validated conversion and must match the NSI acquisition, surface, parcellation and preprocessing assumptions.
